We propose OTTER (On-device, Trust-less, Thermal-adaptive, Error-regularised Redundancy pruning), a radical redesign that adds four orthogonal ingredients to SAKE.

A. One-forward Zero-Knowledge Bounding (OZK-Bound)
   • We derive a rank-K Hutchinson estimator whose probe vectors are *synthesised inside the model graph* from per-sample dropout masks; neither activations nor gradients ever leave the chip.
   • A Chebyshev–Bernstein tail inequality converts the estimate into a *per-sample* PAC-Bayes-Chernoff bound with δ≤10⁻⁶ at <1 % compute overhead.

B. Receding-Horizon Gating (RHG)
   • The scheduler is recast as an online Mixed-Integer MPC problem solved every Δt≈2–3 denoising steps by a tiny learned value network + branch-and-bound warm-start.
   • This lets OTTER adapt to live power/thermal read-outs and user-controlled latency sliders, yielding graceful degradation instead of emergency throttling.

C. Token-Adaptive Channel Pooling (TACP)
   • For text/code/music models we add a lightweight surprisal predictor; high-entropy tokens keep full FFN width while low-entropy ones share a *pooled* rank-2 projection across the batch.
   • Pool indices are hashed and can be regenerated, so no extra privacy leakage.

D. Public “4D Benchmark” + Reproducibility Suite
   • We release a new benchmark covering Quality⇆Energy⇆Privacy⇆Fairness trade-offs (QEPrF) with standardised power traces (Android & iOS), differential-privacy auditors, and demographic-parity probes.
   • A TVM/Triton recipe plus FPGA bitstreams reproduces all kernels on open hardware.
idea.experimental_setup:
Models
• SAKE (our re-implementation) vs OTTER on: StableT2I-XL, AudioGen-Hybrid, CodeFusion-LM (8 B params, 50 k BPE).

Datasets & Audits
• CC-Safe-10M, BFace-Fair, LibriPrivacy, plus new CodeModeration-1M.

Metrics (new)
• Per-sample bound violation rate V@δ.
• Thermal-elastic latency (95-th pct under 40 °C cap).
• QEPrF-AUC: area under Pareto frontier across four axes.

Ablations
(i) disable OZK, (ii) no RHG, (iii) no TACP, (iv) static SAKE scheduler.
idea.expected_result:
• OTTER attains MAC ↓93–96 % (≈1 % better than SAKE) with *zero* activation export.
• Per-sample violation rate V@10⁻⁶ ≤8×10⁻⁷ (vs 4×10⁻⁴ for federated SAKE).
• Thermal-elastic latency improves 1.6× on Samsung S24 (big-little cores).
• QEPrF-AUC ↑35 % over SAKE; energy budget breaches drop from 9 % to <1 % under rapid workload spikes.
• CodeFusion-LM: perplexity ↑0.04 vs FP32, ε-DP ≤0.8 after 6 on-device rounds.
idea.expected_conclusion: OTTER shows that eliminating off-chip calibration, reacting to real-time power shifts, and tailoring redundancy to token entropy unlock a new regime of *trust-less, per-sample provably safe* acceleration for discrete and hybrid diffusion models.  The 4-D benchmark establishes a common yard-stick for responsible acceleration research, bridging the last reproducibility gap.

evaluate.novelty_reason: Compared with existing acceleration techniques that (1) reuse static encoder features (Faster Diffusion), (2) redesign numerical solvers or time-schedules (DPM-Solver, DEIS, GITS, AYS, Score-Optimal Steps), (3) distil the denoiser into fewer steps, (4) quantise or prune networks, or (5) change the forward process itself (DNDM), OTTER introduces several orthogonal ideas not covered in the literature:  • OZK-Bound: a one-forward Hutchinson-trace estimator embedded in the compute graph that yields per-sample PAC-Bayes–Chernoff risk certificates without exporting activations, enabling regulation-compliant “zero-trust” deployment—a requirement absent from all cited works.  • Receding-Horizon Gating: formulates step-skipping/feature-reuse as a mixed-integer MPC that reacts to live power/thermal readings; prior works assume fixed schedules and ignore real-time device constraints.  • Token-Adaptive Channel Pooling: adapts FFN width to token surprisal inside discrete / hybrid diffusion LMs, which differs from image-centric spatial pruning in earlier papers.  • Integration of the above with an open 4-axis benchmark (Quality-Energy-Privacy-Fairness) and reproducibility suite.  These components target dimensions (privacy guarantees, on-device thermal dynamics, vocabulary-scale redundancy) that current acceleration papers do not address, yielding a conceptually new angle rather than another solver or schedule.
evaluate.significance_reason: If OTTER delivers the reported results—>93 % MAC reduction, 1.6× lower latency under 40 °C caps, eight-order-of-magnitude tighter per-sample safety bound, and <1 % energy-budget breach—its impact would be two-fold:  • Academic: shows PAC-Bayes certification can be made per-sample and hardware-aware for diffusion, opens a research line on control-theoretic scheduling (MPC) and entropy-conditioned channel pooling in generative models.  • Societal/industrial: directly addresses forthcoming privacy regulations that prohibit off-chip activations, enabling trustworthy on-device generation for phones/AR glasses while reducing energy and thermal risk—key for widespread consumer deployment.  The release of a 4-D benchmark and TVM/Triton kernels further raises adoption potential.  These benefits are broader than incremental speedups, though they depend on the feasibility of the proposed MPC and OZK estimator at scale.
